mechanisms.name: `--enable-annotation-validation` enabled by default (#11819)
resourcesConsumers: validating admission webhook (CREATE and UPDATE of ingresses, `failurePolicy: Fail`)
mechanisms.mechanism: The 1.12.0 binary enables annotation validation by default, so annotations with invalid values are rejected. This also takes effect in the validating webhook, which is enabled here. Chart 4.12.0 flips `controller.enableAnnotationValidations` to `true`, but the rendered args don't contain the flag, so the behaviour comes from the binary default. That default is still on, so the unchanged args don't mean nothing changes.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The Ingress has one annotation, `ssl-redirect: "false"`. It is low risk and has a plain boolean value, which is valid. No annotation in the repo is rejected by the validation.
citedEvidence: rendered diff shows no `--enable-annotation-validation` arg added
assumptions: The repo is the complete declaration, so this is the only Ingress (per ORIENTATION)
This is a static review; live cluster state was not checked
missingEvidence: Live cluster state, including any Ingresses not declared in this repo, and later UPDATEs that the new controller would validate
Ingresses on other clusters that share `values.yaml`
recommendedValidation: Apply the rendered Ingress on staging or with `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` against a 1.12.0 controller and confirm the webhook admits it
Check the new controller logs for validation or "dropping ingress" errors
Check that `ssl-redirect: "false"` is still honored (HTTP returns 200, no 308)
Watch that the admission jobs complete, because a broken webhook with `failurePolicy: Fail` blocks every Ingress write in the cluster

mechanisms.name: `allow-cross-namespace-resources` disabled by default (#11819)
mechanisms.mechanism: Annotations that reference a Secret or ConfigMap in another namespace (`auth-secret`, `auth-tls-secret`, `proxy-ssl-secret` and similar) are no longer allowed.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: The Ingress has none of these annotations. Both backends are Services in the same `docs` namespace, and backends are not subject to this option anyway. There is no TLS section and no default SSL certificate arg. The controller and the Ingress are in different namespaces, but no resource is referenced across namespaces.
citedEvidence: values.yaml / values-prod.yaml have no `allow-cross-namespace-resources` and no `default-ssl-certificate`
assumptions: The repo is the complete declaration (per ORIENTATION)
missingEvidence: Ingresses in the cluster that are not declared in this repo, which may carry cross-namespace annotations
Ingresses on other clusters that share `values.yaml`
recommendedValidation: After the rollout, run `kubectl get ingress -A -o yaml | grep -E 'snippet|auth-|secret'` and confirm no Ingress outside `docs` uses risky or cross-namespace annotations
Confirm that no other cluster in the Argo setup has Ingresses that depend on the old defaults

mechanisms.name: `annotations-risk-level` lowered to High (#11819)
mechanisms.mechanism: Annotations rated Critical, such as `server-snippet`, `configuration-snippet` and `auth-snippet`, are no longer accepted.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: None of these annotations are used, and `ssl-redirect` is low risk. `allow-snippet-annotations: "false"` disappears from the rendered ConfigMap only because the chart no longer emits a value that was already the default. That is not a behaviour change and is a different change from #11819.
citedEvidence: removal of `allow-snippet-annotations: "false"` from the rendered ConfigMap (chart `allowSnippetAnnotations: false`)
assumptions: The repo is the complete declaration (per ORIENTATION)
missingEvidence: Ingresses in the cluster that are not declared in this repo, which may carry snippet annotations
Ingresses on other clusters that share `values.yaml`
recommendedValidation: After the rollout, run `kubectl get ingress -A -o yaml | grep -E 'snippet|auth-|secret'` and confirm no Ingress outside `docs` uses risky annotations
Confirm that no other cluster in the Argo setup has Ingresses that depend on the old defaults

mechanisms.name: `strict-validate-path-type` enabled by default (#11819)
mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: not affected (high confidence, not verified against source)
mechanisms.mechanism: The admission webhook enforces a character whitelist on Exact and Prefix paths. `/.well-known` is the only path with unusual characters and is the most plausible place for a problem.
mechanisms.mitigationOrNoExposure: From the author's recollection, which was not verified against source, the allowed set is alphanumerics plus `- . _ ~ /`, so `.` and `-` pass. The request path `/.well-known/security.txt` still maps to the file, and path validation does not change that.
citedEvidence: recollection of `internal/ingress/inspector/rules.go` (source not in the upstream folder)
assumptions: The allowed character set is as the author recalls (not verified against source)
missingEvidence: The exact path-validation regex, because the upstream folder doesn't include `rules.go`
recommendedValidation: Apply the rendered Ingress on staging or with `kubectl apply --dry-run=server` against a 1.12.0 controller and confirm the webhook admits it (this closes the path-regex uncertainty)
Confirm `curl -H 'Host: docs.example.com'` for `/`, `/.well-known/security.txt` and a 404 path returns as before

mechanisms.claimedClassQuote: could matter if the image's filesystem permissions (e.g. mounted volumes) assume another group
mechanisms.mechanism: The controller's `runAsGroup: 82` could matter if the image's filesystem permissions, such as mounted volumes, assume another group.

overall.recommendation: Proceed with conditions. The upgrade is not expected to break this environment, but the staging/dry-run admission test, the post-rollout checks, the webhook and admission-job checks, and the other-cluster check should be done first. `targetRevision` should be updated to 4.12.0 only after those.
overall.quote: Not expected to break this environment.
